CorMethod#summary.en: Correlation coefficient: Pearson's r, Kendall's tau or Spearman's rho.

CorUse#summary.en: Handling of missing values, as R's `use`.

CutOptions.includeLowest#summary.en: Close the first interval on the left (or the last on the right when `right` is false). Default `false`.

CutOptions.right#summary.en: Intervals closed on the right, (a, b] (default `true`); otherwise [a, b).

DiffOptions.differences#summary.en: Number of times differences are taken. Default `1`.

DiffOptions.lag#summary.en: Distance between the values subtracted. Default `1`.

FindIntervalOptions.allInside#summary.en: Give 1 instead of 0 left of the first point and N - 1 instead of N at or right of the last (N = `vec.length`).

FindIntervalOptions.rightmostClosed#summ.en: Treat the last interval as closed on the right (with `leftOpen`, the first as closed on the left).

HistOptions.breaks#summary.en:
Break points (finite: an infinite or NaN one is an error), a number of cells (a suggestion for pretty), or a
rule: `"Sturges"` (default), `"Scott"` or `"FD"` (Freedman-Diaconis).

HistOptions.includeLowest#summary.en: Close the first cell on the left (the last on the right when `right` is false). Default `true`.

HistOptions.right#summary.en: Cells closed on the right, (a, b] (default `true`).

HistResult.breaks#summary.en: The cell boundaries, one more than the cells.

HistResult.counts#summary.en: Number of values in each cell.

IQR#summary.en: Interquartile range, the difference of the 0.75 and 0.25 quantiles. Equivalent to R's `IQR()`.

MadOptions.center#summary.en: Centre. Default: the median (`NaN` if `x` has a missing value and `naRm` is not set).

MadOptions.constant#summary.en: Scale factor. Default `1.4826` (consistent for the normal standard deviation).

MadOptions.high#summary.en: For an even count n, take the higher one (the "hi-median"): the (n / 2 + 1)-th smallest, as for `low`. Both `low` and `high` is an error for an even count.

MadOptions.low#summary.en:
For an even count n, take the lower of the two middle absolute deviations (the "lo-median"): the (n / 2)-th
smallest. As in R, n counts the missing values unless `naRm` removed them, the k-th smallest is taken among
the deviations that are not missing, and fewer than k of them (or k = 0) is an error. With an odd count the
ordinary median is used.

MeanADOptions.center#summary.en: Centre: the mean (default) or `"median"`, or a number.

MeanOptions.trim#summary.en: Fraction (0 to 0.5) of values trimmed from each end before the mean. Default `0`.

NaRmOptions#summary.en: Options of the summaries that can drop missing values.

NaRmOptions.naRm#summary.en: Drop `NaN` (R's `NA`) before computing. Default `false`: a `NaN` gives `NaN`.

PrettyOptions.highUBias#summary.en: Bias towards larger units. Default `1.5`. Must be finite and non-negative (as in R).

PrettyOptions.minN#summary.en:
Minimal number of intervals. Default `n / 3` rounded down (computed from `n` before it is truncated). Truncated
towards 0 to an integer (as in R); `NaN`, a negative value or one greater than `n` is an error.

PrettyOptions.n#summary.en:
Desired number of intervals. Default `5`. Truncated towards 0 to an integer (as in R); `NaN`, a negative value
or one of 2^31 or more in absolute value is an error (unless `x` has no finite values).

PrettyOptions.shrinkSml#summary.en: Factor applied to the cell when the range is very small. Default `0.75`. Must be finite and positive (as in R).

PrettyOptions.u5Bias#summary.en:
Bias towards 5 over 2 times a power of 10. Default `0.5 + 1.5 * highUBias`. Must be finite and non-negative (as
in R).

QuantileOptions.type#summary.en: Hyndman and Fan's definition, 1 to 9. Default `7`.

RankOptions.naLast#summary.en:
Missing values: `"last"` (default, R's `na.last = TRUE`) ranks them after the others, `"first"` (`FALSE`) before
them, `"keep"` leaves them `NaN`.

ScaleOptions.center#summary.en: Subtract the column means (`true`, default), nothing (`false`) or the given values.

ScaleOptions.scale#summary.en:
Divide by the root mean square of each (centred) column, sqrt(sum v^2 / (n - 1)) (`true`, default: the standard
deviation when centred), by nothing (`false`) or by the given values.

TableOptions.useNA#summary.en: Count missing values: `"no"` (default), `"ifany"` (when there are some) or `"always"`.

TabulateOptions.nbins#summary.en: Number of bins. Default max(1, bin); truncated towards 0, as R does.

TiesMethod#summary.en: How ties are ranked, as R's `ties.method`.

cor(0)#summary.en:
Correlation of two vectors, or correlation matrix of the columns of a matrix (or between the columns of `x` and
`y`). Equivalent to R's `cor()`. Pearson correlations are computed in double-double, so they can be slightly more
accurate than R's (exactly 1 for perfectly correlated data).

cor(1)#summary.en:
Correlation of two vectors, or correlation matrix of the columns of a matrix (or between the columns of `x` and
`y`). Equivalent to R's `cor()`. Pearson correlations are computed in double-double, so they can be slightly more
accurate than R's (exactly 1 for perfectly correlated data).

cov(0)#summary.en:
Covariance of two vectors, or covariance matrix of the columns of a matrix (or between the columns of `x` and `y`).
Equivalent to R's `cov()`.

cov(1)#summary.en:
Covariance of two vectors, or covariance matrix of the columns of a matrix (or between the columns of `x` and `y`).
Equivalent to R's `cov()`.

cummax#summary.en: Running maxima. Equivalent to R's `cummax()`. `NaN` from the first `NaN` on.

cumprod#summary.en:
Running products. Equivalent to R's `cumprod()`. Products beyond the double range show as ±Infinity with the right
sign, as R's long double accumulator does.

cumsum#summary.en:
Running sums. Equivalent to R's `cumsum()`. Each partial sum is rounded from an exact accumulator; `NaN` from the
first `NaN` on.

cut#@param breaks.en:
The break points (NaN among them is dropped, as R does; fewer than 2 left are an error), or a
  number of intervals (at least 2): then equal intervals over the range of `x`, widened by 1/1000 of the range at
  each end, as R does. That range must be finite.

cut#summary.en: Interval numbers (1-based) of the values, or NaN outside the breaks. Equivalent to R's `cut(..., labels = FALSE)`.

cv#summary.en: Coefficient of variation sd / mean (sample standard deviation). Equivalent to `DescTools::CoefVar()` in R.

diff#summary.en:
Lagged and iterated differences. Equivalent to R's `diff()`. For a vector (empty when `lag * differences` is at
least the length).

ecdf#summary.en:
Empirical distribution function of `x`: a function returning the fraction of values at or below its argument.
Equivalent to R's `ecdf()`. `NaN` values are dropped.

findInterval#summary.en:
For each value, the number of break points at or below it (the interval index). Equivalent to R's
`findInterval()`. `vec` must be non-decreasing.

fivenum#summary.en:
Tukey's five-number summary (minimum, lower hinge, median, upper hinge, maximum). Equivalent to R's `fivenum()`.
`NaN` values are dropped.

geometricMean#summary.en:
Geometric mean exp(mean(log x)). Equivalent to `DescTools::Gmean()` in R. NaN with a negative value, 0 with a
zero.

hist#summary.en:
Histogram counts. Equivalent to R's `hist(x, plot = FALSE)`. Break points (by default pretty points over the range
with about Sturges' number of cells), counts, densities and cell midpoints. Non-finite values are dropped.

kurtosis#summary.en:
Sample excess kurtosis. Equivalent to `e1071::kurtosis()` in R. Missing values are dropped; `{ type: 1 }` is
jStat's kurtosis.

mad#summary.en: Median absolute deviation, scaled. Equivalent to R's `mad()`.

mean#summary.en:
Arithmetic mean, optionally trimmed. Equivalent to R's `mean()`. Accurate to the last bit: the sum is taken in
double-double and corrected by the mean deviation, as R corrects its long double mean.

meanAD#summary.en: Mean absolute deviation from the centre. Equivalent to `DescTools::MeanAD()` in R. Missing values are dropped.

median#summary.en: Median of the values (the mean of the two middle ones for an even count). Equivalent to R's `median()`.

modes#summary.en:
The most frequent values (all of them, in increasing order) and their frequency. Equivalent to
`DescTools::Mode()` in R. Missing values are dropped; `value` is `[NaN]` and `frequency` NaN when every value
occurs once.

modes.frequency#summary.en: How often each of them occurs (NaN when every value occurs once).

modes.value#summary.en: The most frequent values, in increasing order (`[NaN]` when every value occurs once).

pretty#summary.en:
About n + 1 equally spaced "round" values (1, 2 or 5 times a power of 10) covering the range of `x`. Equivalent to
R's `pretty()`.

prod#summary.en: Product of the values. Equivalent to R's `prod()`. 1 for an empty vector.

quantile(0)#@param probs.en: Probabilities in [0, 1]. Default `[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]`. A single number gives a single number.

quantile(0)#summary.en: Sample quantiles. Equivalent to R's `quantile()`. Without names (R's `names = FALSE`).

quantile(1)#@param probs.en: Probabilities in [0, 1]. Default `[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]`. A single number gives a single number.

quantile(1)#summary.en: Sample quantiles. Equivalent to R's `quantile()`. Without names (R's `names = FALSE`).

range#summary.en:
`[min, max]` of the values. Equivalent to R's `range()`. `[NaN, NaN]` with a missing value unless `naRm`;
`[Infinity, -Infinity]` for an empty vector.

scale#summary.en:
Centre and scale the columns of a matrix (array of rows; a vector is one column). Equivalent to R's `scale()`.
`center` and `scale` report the values used (R's attributes), when any.

scale.center#summary.en: The values subtracted from each column (R's `scaled:center` attribute); absent with `center: false`.

scale.scale#summary.en: The values each column was divided by (R's `scaled:scale` attribute); absent with `scale: false`.

scale.scaled#summary.en: The centred and scaled matrix, as an array of rows (R's returned matrix).

sd#summary.en: Sample standard deviation (denominator n - 1). Equivalent to R's `sd()`.

skewness#summary.en:
Sample skewness. Equivalent to `e1071::skewness()` in R. Missing values are dropped; `{ type: 1 }` is jStat's
skewness.

sum#summary.en: Sum of the values. Equivalent to R's `sum()`. For a numeric vector (0 for an empty one).

table#summary.en:
Frequency table of the distinct values. Equivalent to R's `table()`. For one numeric vector: `values` in increasing
order (NaN last when counted) with their `counts`. As in R, values with the same text (15 significant digits, as
R's `as.character`) are counted as one, under the smallest of them.

table.values#summary.en: The distinct values, in increasing order (NaN last when missing values are counted); R's names.

tabulate(0)#summary.en:
Counts of the integers 1..nbins in `bin` (values truncated towards 0; others, NaN, infinite values and values
beyond the integer range of R are not counted).
Equivalent to R's `tabulate()`. `nbins` defaults to max(1, bin) and is truncated towards 0, as R does; it is the
second argument or the option `nbins` (giving both is a RangeError).

tabulate(1)#summary.en: Counts of the integers 1..nbins in `bin`, with the number of bins in the options: `tabulate(bin, { nbins: 3 })`.

unique#summary.en: Distinct values in order of first appearance (one NaN at most). Equivalent to R's `unique()`.

variance#summary.en:
Sample variance (denominator n - 1). Equivalent to R's `var()`. For a vector (`NaN` for fewer than 2 values); named
`variance` because `var` cannot be a name in JavaScript. For matrices use `cov`.

weightedMean#summary.en:
Weighted mean `sum(x w) / sum(w)`. Equivalent to R's `weighted.mean()`. Values with weight 0 do not enter the
numerator (even if infinite or NaN), and `naRm` drops missing values of `x` with their weights.
